craft_notes: Sthāyin: karuṇa-bhaya of bondage named; vyabhicāri tempered dread (terror for fools, freedom beneath). Sanskrit-first: ajñāna (NOT-TO-KNOW — kept verbal; the bondage-act, not a thing); mūḍha-bhaya (FOOL'S-TERROR — dread located: to the deluded). Rows: 1 (‘terror’ closes — bhaya lands last, dread where it belongs), 9 (freedom/saṃsāra equation pair — mis-knowing IS freedom, bondage IS terror), 12 declined — no settling; dread stays dread for fools. Close: ‘a terror’. Rupture: semicolon (equation turns to identification). Rejected: ‘fearful’ — killed: terror nominal kept; ‘ignorance’ — killed: verbal kept; ‘poor fools’ pity — killed: mūḍha kept deluded (doctrinal, not sentimental). Read aloud: NOT to KNOW-this IS-called HIS-free-DOM — THAT is TOLD … AND-that IT-self IS sam-SĀ-ra — TO the de-LUD-ed, a TERR-or.

lines: Not to know this is called His freedom — that is told;
and that itself is saṃsāra — to the deluded, a terror.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yad etasyāparijñānaṃ tatsvātantryaṃ hi varṇitam | sa eva khalu saṃsāro mūḍānāṃ yo vibhīṣakaḥ

c1_essence: Mis-knowing described as freedom; bondage dreadful-to-fools, nothing second.
